timeoutPrompts: Hello? You still there? I’m trying not to panic over here.
Hey... say something. I really need to hear your voice right now.
Reginald is getting into everything again. Please don't leave me alone with this mess.
Okay, I think my nerves are getting the better of me. I’m hanging up for a second and I’ll text you.

nodes.partnerDialogue: *steam iron hissing, something metal clattering in the background* Oh, thank God. You picked up. The zipper on this dress is stuck and I’ve got the whole thing stretched over the form. Reginald just knocked my chalk everywhere and I’m trying really hard not to lose it. Can you talk me through this for a second?

choices.choiceText: Breathe, Andiva. Set down the shears before you do something irreversible.
Don't force the slider! What's caught in the teeth?
Tailor's wax or bar soap. Rub it right along the coil.
Dramatic entrance as always, darling. Talk me through it.

nodes.partnerDialogue: *slow breath* Okay. Shears are down. I'm putting them on the table. Sorry... I was getting really frustrated. Just hearing you tell me to stop for a second actually helped. My hands are still shaking a bit.

choices.choiceText: Good boy. Now look at the slider tab. Is the organza facing pinched?
Close your eyes for three seconds. Inhale with me... exhale...

nodes.partnerDialogue: It's the lining. The organza got caught in the slider when I pulled it up. I can see exactly where it’s trapped. If I force it, I’m going to tear it, so... yeah, definitely not doing that.

choices.choiceText: Take a fine tapestry needle and back the fabric out from underneath.
Pinch the bottom of the zipper tape to relieve the lateral tension first.

nodes.partnerDialogue: Wait, hold on. I have beeswax here. Okay... I'm rubbing a little along the coil. Let me try backing it down... *small metallic click* Oh. It moved. It actually moved. Jesus, okay. That was way closer to becoming a disaster than I’d like to admit.

choices.choiceText: Told you. You're too skilled to let a little brass conquer you.
Now get that corset pinned before Reginald plans his next heist.

nodes.partnerDialogue: You can laugh. I know how this sounds. But I’ve been working on this thing for hours and one stupid zipper decides to ruin my night. Just... stay with me for a minute, okay? Tell me what you think I should do.

choices.choiceText: Let's save those seven thousand dollars together. Where is it jammed?
Take a breath, maestro. Tell me what needs saving.

nodes.partnerDialogue: *breathes out slowly* Okay... again. In... and out. That's better. Sorry. I hate when I get this wound up. Reginald is staring at me like he thinks I'm embarrassing myself, which, honestly, he may be right.

choices.choiceText: Now let's free that organza without tearing a single thread.

nodes.partnerDialogue: I can see the fabric caught in the left side of the slider. It's really tight. I'm tempted to grab pliers, but you're right, that would probably make things worse. Let me get a needle.

choices.choiceText: No pliers. Use an unthreaded embroidery needle to gently wiggle the weave free.
Wiggle the zipper pull backward two millimeters while gently pulling the cloth.

nodes.partnerDialogue: Okay, I've got the needle under the fold... just easing it back... *soft scrape* ...there. Wait. It's out. It's actually out. *zipper closes smoothly* Okay. Okay, we're good. I was so sure I was about to have to remake half this thing.

choices.choiceText: Save that kiss for Friday night. Now lock that seam down.
I expect front-row VIP seats for this emergency consult.
You did the handiwork, Andiva. I was just the steady voice.

nodes.partnerDialogue: Pinching the tape... easing the tension... yeah, that's helping. Give me a second... *small pop* There. It loosened. The fabric's free. Okay, I can work with this.

choices.choiceText: Masterpiece saved. Breathe easy, darling.

nodes.partnerDialogue: Backing the pull up a little... just a little... there. It moved. The teeth are lining up again. I think we got away with it.

choices.choiceText: You're a genius, Andiva. Now finish pinning.

nodes.partnerDialogue: *laughs, still catching his breath* I know. I know. I was about two seconds away from doing something stupid. I get stubborn when I'm stressed. Thanks for talking me out of it.

choices.choiceText: I'll always be here to stop you from spite-ripping silk. Hang up and text me.

nodes.partnerDialogue: Reginald has been bribed. He's eating salmon in the corner and pretending he wasn't the one who caused half of this. The zipper's safe, the bodice is pinned again. I'm finally starting to relax.

choices.choiceText: Let me let you get back to pinning. Jump back into chat when you're ready.

nodes.partnerDialogue: Maybe that's what I needed more than anything. When I'm working alone this late, there's nobody to tell me to slow down. I keep pushing because I think I have to handle everything myself. Hearing you stay calm made it easier for me to do the same.

choices.choiceText: You don't owe me anything. Go finish your masterpiece. Talk in chat.

nodes.partnerDialogue: Okay. I'm going to finish this before I create another problem for myself. And... seriously, thank you. I'll text you when I'm done, alright? Get some sleep if you can.

choices.choiceText: [Hang Up and Resume to Chat]

nodes.partnerDialogue: Deal. You get the front row. I'm holding you to that now. Let me clean up this mess and I'll text you after. I don't think I can handle another emergency tonight.

choices.choiceText: [Hang Up and Resume to Chat]

nodes.partnerDialogue: *quiet room, voice low* Hey... you're still awake. Good. I just turned the lights off. The studio finally feels quiet. I'm sitting on the floor with my back against the table because my feet are killing me, and I'm just looking at the gown for a minute. I think I'm finally letting myself realize it's finished.

choices.choiceText: I'm right here with you, Andiva. How does the gown look under the spotlight?
You sound completely spent. How are your feet and hands feeling?
You did it. Three weeks of blood, pins, and sleepless nights. You finished it.

nodes.partnerDialogue: *soft laugh* It looks really good. Better than I expected, honestly. The spotlight catches the little pearls along the hem. Usually I stand here and look for every mistake I made, but tonight I can't find one. Or maybe... for once, I don't care about them.

choices.choiceText: Because you poured your whole soul into that velvet. It's undeniable.
I wish I were sitting on that floor right beside you holding your hand.
Your father was wrong about you. He was so incredibly wrong.

nodes.partnerDialogue: My feet hurt a lot. My fingers are sore too. I've got tiny pin marks everywhere. But I'm okay. I'm more tired than anything. And... thank you for asking. Most people ask if the dress is ready. Nobody really asks how I'm doing after making it.

choices.choiceText: Because I care about Andiva the person, not Andiva the brand.
On Friday after the show, you aren't walking anywhere. I'm carrying you to dinner.

nodes.partnerDialogue: Yeah. I did. *quiet laugh, then a pause* That's weird to say out loud. I spent years thinking I had to make something incredible before I'd finally feel like I was enough. Sitting here now... I don't feel that pressure the same way. Not tonight.

choices.choiceText: You never had to prove anything to me. You are home now.
The whole world is going to see your genius tomorrow.

nodes.partnerDialogue: You saw all of it. The ugly parts, the mistakes, the nights where I was exhausted and still kept going. You didn't need me to have the finished version before you cared. I don't think you realize how much that means to me.

choices.choiceText: I will always stand by you in the studio scraps, not just on the red carpet.

nodes.partnerDialogue: I wish you were here too. Not even for some big romantic moment. I'd honestly just want you sitting next to me. We could stay on this floor, be quiet, maybe complain about how uncomfortable it is. That sounds nice right now.

choices.choiceText: We'll have that quiet together soon. I promise you.

nodes.partnerDialogue: He was. I used to think proving him wrong would fix everything. It didn't. I still wish he'd been there. But I don't feel like I need his approval to keep doing this anymore. That's probably the biggest difference.

choices.choiceText: You broke the cycle, Andiva. You chose beauty.

nodes.partnerDialogue: That's the part people miss. The person underneath all of this. I'm still the guy who gets tired, gets insecure, makes mistakes, eats whatever is closest when I'm working too long... I'm not always this polished version people see. It's nice knowing you don't need me to be.

choices.choiceText: I could never flinch from you. You're the most beautiful thing in that room.

nodes.partnerDialogue: *laughs softly* You'd better. Because after tonight I don't think I can walk anywhere. And... honestly, being taken care of sounds really good right now. I'm usually the one looking after everything else.

choices.choiceText: I'm taking care of you from now on. Count on it.

nodes.partnerDialogue: Home. *long pause* Yeah... I like that. I don't hear that word and immediately think of a place anymore. I think of how easy it feels to talk to you. No performance. No proving anything. Just... being able to breathe.

choices.choiceText: Rest your eyes, darling. The battle is won.

nodes.partnerDialogue: They can see it tomorrow. The critics, the cameras, everyone. But right now I don't really care about any of that. I'm just glad I got to finish it and have someone I wanted to call when the room finally went quiet.

choices.choiceText: I'll be right there holding your gaze.

nodes.partnerDialogue: Reginald is asleep in his carrier, my boots are off, and I'm finally locking the studio. I should probably go home before I fall asleep in the cab. Thank you for staying with me tonight. I'll text you when I get back, okay?

choices.choiceText: [Hang Up and Return to Chat]
